subject: Request: service concession for Nivara — temporary latency tolerance & credits cap
messages:
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@nivara-health.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Hale <tom.hale@nivara-health.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: short-term SLO concession and credits cap for onboarding

Priyom — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Nivara is excited to onboard Redwood for our clinical summarization endpoint, but two procurement constraints popped up on our side today: budget headroom for Dedicated capacity is tighter than we expected, and our legal team is asking us to limit exposure to vendor service credits while we run an internal pilot.

Concretely, they have asked if Redwood can: 1) allow a temporary latency/uptime tolerance (we can accept up to 99.5% monthly uptime for the first 12 months instead of 99.9%), and 2) cap potential monthly service-credit liability to 5% of monthly fees during that period.

We know this is outside standard terms — please let us know if there’s a path to agree (discount/credit offset, dedicated pool sizing, or alternative remedies) so we can move forward before our board meeting next week. Attaching our mutual action plan and a short observability snapshot.

— Sara
Director of Engineering, Nivara Health
Attachments: Nivara_Mutual_Action_Plan_v3.pdf, latency_observability_snapshot_20261129.csv

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 18:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: short-term SLO concession and credits cap for onboarding

Team — forwarding Nivara's ask. TL;DR: customer requests a 12-month concession to allow 99.5% uptime (vs our standard 99.9%) and to cap service-credit liability at 5% of monthly fees for that period. They're on a modern open-model stack and want to avoid overprovisioning costs during pilot.

Proposed commercial mitigations I think we can offer:
- Limit the concession to a single namespace/endpoint (clinical-summarizer-prod) and to the first 12 months after go-live.
- Require a minimum 6‑month reserved capacity commit or a queue of usage milestones (so we get predictability).
- Cap the aggregate monthly service credit at 5% of invoice, and make credits ineligible for partial latency variances (only apply for sustained availability breaches per our measurement window).
- Add enhanced observability and a scheduled QBR at month 3 to re-evaluate SLO.

Ask: can Deal Desk + Exec signoff approve the above as a one-off concession with these guardrails? If yes, I can route a short amendment + DocuSign. Need a yes/no and any additional conditions by EOD tomorrow (11/30) to keep Nivara on track.

— Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: short-term SLO concession and credits cap for onboarding

Priyom — thanks for the clear proposal. A few clarifying points before I recommend approval to Lauren:
1) Measurement window: confirm we use monthly rolling window by customer namespace and our standard incident taxonomy. No credits for degraded latency unless we hit an availability breach as defined in the draft amendment.
2) Financial cap: 5% monthly cap is acceptable provided we also include a hard cap of $25k per month for the first 12 months (Nivara's expected spend suggests this is reasonable).
3) Mitigations: require dedicated placement on a medium reserved pool (customer pays for reserved capacity for at least 6 months) and an explicit P0 handoff matrix for incident response.

If the customer signs to these guardrails I recommend approval with one exec condition: limit the concession to a maximum of one renewal cycle (12 months) and put a mandatory SLO re-eval at month 9.

I’ll draft a short amendment and include the $25k cap and observability commitments. Lauren — can we get signoff on approving this exception under those terms?

— Marissa
Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Request: short-term SLO concession and credits cap for onboarding

Approved with conditions. Summary of decision:
- Approve temporary uptime tolerance change to 99.5% (monthly) limited to the clinical-summarizer-prod namespace for 12 months.
- Approve monthly service-credit cap of 5% of monthly fees, with an absolute cap of $25,000/month for the concession period.
- Credits apply only to sustained availability breaches per the amendment; latency degradations alone do not trigger credits unless they meet availability criteria in our measurement window.
- Require customer to commit to 6 months of reserved capacity (medium pool) or equivalent capacity-based billing for the pilot.
- Add mandatory SLO re-eval at month 9 and a QBR at month 3.

Legal to produce a 1-page amendment with these specifics and a DocuSign link. Compose as a limited one-off concession: not precedent-setting and does not change our global SLA. Aditya — please confirm pricing offset (if any) — my default is to allow up to a 10% commercial discount to assist with onboarding if needed, but pricing team to sign off.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@nivara-health.com>, Tom Hale <tom.hale@nivara-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term SLO concession and credits cap for onboarding

Sara / Tom — great news: we have exec approval to proceed with a limited concession. Key points (excerpt from approved terms):
- Temporary uptime tolerance: 99.5% monthly for the clinical-summarizer-prod namespace for 12 months.
- Monthly service-credit liability capped at 5% of your monthly fees, with an absolute cap of $25,000/month during the concession period.
- Credits only apply to sustained availability breaches as defined in the amendment; transient latency variances will not trigger credits.
- Requirement: 6-month reserved capacity commit (medium pool) or equivalent billing that ensures baseline capacity.
- Mandatory check-ins: QBR at month 3 and SLO re-eval at month 9.

I’ve attached the draft amendment and a DocuSign link — Legal will send the formal doc this afternoon. If you’re comfortable with these terms I can route for signature and schedule onboarding next week.

Thanks for working through this together — excited to get Nivara onboarded.

— Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: Nivara_Mutual_Action_Plan_v3.pdf, latency_observability_snapshot_20261129.csv
